title: @Cacheable does nothing, then serves stale data once it works
summary: Adding @EnableCaching turns the cache on, then update and delete write back and evict the same key.

turns.user: put @Cacheable on the product lookup but the log still shows a select every single time. is the cache even on?

assistant.body: It is not, because nothing enables it. @Cacheable on its own is only a marker. @EnableCaching is what makes Spring wrap the bean in a caching proxy. With no cache library on the classpath, Spring Boot then sets up a simple CacheManager backed by a ConcurrentHashMap. Let's add one line to the application class.

turns.user: ok that works. now if i change a price in the admin screen the detail page keeps the old one until restart

assistant.body: Note: the cache has no idea the database changed. Update writes the fresh value back with @CachePut, and delete removes it with @CacheEvict. The key is the part that bites. Leave it out and Spring builds the key from every argument, so update(id, request) writes to SimpleKey(id, request) while find(id) keeps reading the old entry under plain id. Both get key = "#id" to line up with find.
